cases.note: An unbarred sequence is one virtual measure whose slots share the exact bar capacity.
T0 allocates the whole bar to the single undurated slot; U1 never invents a duration of its own.
Rational duration suffixes belong to the T0 grammar; U1 does not narrow them to integers.
A draft section name equal to an existing name warns and still creates a new section; v1 defines no section merge.
Two adjacent boundary tokens deliberately enclose one empty measure; the preview keeps it instead of joining the neighbours.
Two complete measures cannot enter one measure boundary.
The destination measure already holds its complete capacity.
A before/after-event boundary always denotes a non-empty measure, so the complete lane can never target it.
A named-section draft cannot enter a section boundary.
An implicit draft cannot enter the document level; every document section must be named.
A fragment may not mix an implicit sequence with named sections, so the draft refuses and only single-chord recovery remains.
A draft of one empty measure has nothing to place into an empty target measure; the complete lane requires one non-empty measure.
A short bar is a T0 refusal, never a silent partial insertion.
T0 owns syntax classification; U1 preserves its code and range and never substitutes a guessed chord.
Recoverable tokens keep their source text and stay individually insertable while the whole draft refuses.
A lone surrogate refuses inside U1 before T0 is called, because the accepted quick-entry state admits only valid scalar text.
One recovered two-beat chord still fits the two remaining beats.
The destination measure has no remaining capacity, so the single-chord lane is unavailable as well.
T0 could not resolve the duration, so the caller must supply one exact positive beat duration before the single-chord lane commits.
Recovery may use only a measure placement.
A single recovered chord longer than the bar capacity cannot be inserted into an empty measure either.
Exactly 4,095 code points remain inside the draft bound.
Exactly the maximum draft length is accepted by the field and still refused by the grammar.
One code point beyond the bound refuses inside U1 before T0 is called and before any ephemeral intent is dispatched.
Four thousand ninety-six four-byte scalars reach exactly the 16,384 UTF-8 byte bound as well as the code-point bound.
An empty draft is idle: no parse, no plan, no document command.
Clearing a previously ready draft returns the field to idle and dispatches no document command.
Dismissing the preview without activating Insert leaves the ready draft intact and still dispatches no document command.
The draft base revision no longer equals the application revision, so no plan may be claimed.
The stored quick-entry target no longer resolves in the current document.
The field preserves the caller's exact source text, including the comment T0 reports as not round-tripped; U1 never rewrites the draft to its canonical form.
An event annotation is inert data carried through unchanged.
